control.detail: In Augusta, Atlanta and Phoenix there is no city office to stand for and no municipal election to take part in.

producers.reachDetail: Walked: Augusta ME, Atlanta GA, Phoenix AZ, age 40, first morning. Augusta and Atlanta: 'Your town's own government is not in this build yet.' Phoenix: represented, with no manager election recorded.
Imported by its own matrix test and nothing else in src/ or scripts/, so no route can reach it; the walk above confirmed none of its ME, GA or AZ rules appear.

duplication.visibilityDetail: The screen says there is nothing, and a sourced answer exists for the same state.

measurements.at: main at 4965f63c, walked 2026-09-22 ~17:45-18:05Z in Chromium 141 through the ordinary creator
measurements.found: Identical refusal on Campaigns; no city office offered anywhere. The corpus rows for ME, GA and AZ carry ballot, timing, runoff, seat, administration, vacancy, recall, initiative and referendum rules with citations.
measurements.what: Campaigns and Local government screens in three towns

measurements.found: municipal-election-rule-packs-matrix.test.ts and a path string in scripts/prose-corpus/coverage.ts; nothing in play.

notes: The corpus is state baseline law and play asks a per-city question, so wiring it in is a design choice (a baseline where no charter was read), not a repair.
playerReachDetail: A candidate in Maine, Georgia or Arizona is told there is nothing to stand for below governor, while the compiled state law on how their cities elect sits unread.

surface.detail: Politics > Government > Local meetings and records, and the Campaigns screen.

system.detail: Two. Play reads per-government charter readings through municipalRulePackFor in src/simulation/municipal-government.ts. A second, same-named municipalRulePackFor in src/simulation/municipal-election-rule-packs.ts compiles 51 jurisdictions of state baseline municipal election law with statute citations, and only its own test imports it.

title: How a city elects its government
